description:
Give the parent model the same explicit goal-mode entrypoint a human gets from `/bw run`, so an agent that has decomposed and polished an epic can deliberately switch itself into Beadwork's manager-only execution loop instead of merely approximating that behavior with individual ticket and orchestration calls.

## Background

Today `/bw run <epic-id>` is command-only. It validates the host and epic, stores the v1 goal and review policy, arms the standing run appendix, and injects a continuation that tells the parent to refresh Beadwork truth and orchestrate. Models can independently decide to execute an epic, but no tool exposes that state transition. They therefore miss the persistent run-mode policy, interrupted-run semantics, goal conflict protection, automatic goal exit, and the human command's continuation behavior.

## Naming decision

Register **`beadwork_start_goal`** with required `epic_id`.

This is preferable to:

- `beadwork_run_epic`: sounds synchronous or as if the tool itself executes all work; the actual operation is a mode/lifecycle transition.
- `beadwork_impl_epic` / `beadwork_implement_epic`: false ownership semantics—the parent manages dispatch, evidence, review, and ticket lifecycle while children implement.
- `beadwork_enter_goal_mode`: accurate but internal-sounding and less action-oriented.

Tool description should make discovery unambiguous: start Beadwork's manager-only goal mode for an existing open epic and queue the parent continuation that refreshes ready work and orchestrates it. It does not implement the epic synchronously.

## Required behavior

- Input is explicit: `{ epic_id: string }`. Do not infer an epic from conversation, current ready work, or an arbitrary ticket scope.
- Reuse one shared goal-start domain operation with `/bw run`; do not invoke the slash command through synthetic text and do not maintain duplicated validation/state-transition logic.
- Preserve all current `/bw run` checks and effects: active repository, persistent `tui`/`rpc` host, rejected supervisor leftovers, open epic with descendants, one active goal conflict rules, configured review policy, cached prime, persisted scope/goal state, statusline update, and prompt continuation.
- When called during a model turn, queue the existing continuation as `followUp`; the next turn receives the standing run appendix. Do not inject a synthetic same-turn system-prompt mutation.
- Same-epic invocation is idempotent/re-arming: preserve the existing goal identity/start time and queue a fresh continuation. A different live epic rejects without mutating state.
- Return a bounded truthful tool result containing at least epic id/title, goal id, review policy, state `started` or `resumed`, and continuation disposition (`queued_follow_up` or `triggered_turn`). Never claim that implementation, orchestration, or the epic completed.
- Tool errors must throw with actionable messages rather than relying only on TUI notifications; `/bw run` retains human notifications.
- Add the tool to Beadwork parent-tool guidance and operator docs. Teach the model to call it when it has intentionally chosen to execute a ready, already-decomposed epic; do not auto-start merely because an epic exists.

## Interaction with manager-only orchestration

Starting the goal establishes intent and policy; it does not dispatch children itself. On the queued continuation the parent refreshes `beadwork_ready`/`beadwork_show`, starts tickets, composes complete tasks, calls minions `orchestrate`, adjudicates evidence and independent reviews, and closes issues. The parent must not implement delegated scope concurrently.

## Scope / likely files

- `packages/pi-beadwork-extension/src/actions/run.ts`: extract/shared goal-start result and presentation adapters
- `packages/pi-beadwork-extension/src/index.ts`: register `beadwork_start_goal`
- `packages/pi-beadwork-extension/src/prompt.ts`: include the tool and self-initiation boundary
- run/index/prompt and in-process Beadwork/minions tests
- package README and tool/operator documentation

## Acceptance behavior

- A model can call `beadwork_start_goal({ epic_id: "BW-100" })` without a human slash command and the next turn is in the same run mode `/bw run BW-100` would establish.
- Command and tool paths produce equivalent persisted goal/scope/review-policy state and continuation content.
- Calling from a busy agent turn uses follow-up delivery exactly once.
- The tool rejects print/json hosts, inactive repositories, tasks/non-epics, closed/empty epics, supervisor config leftovers, and a conflicting live goal without partial state mutation.
- Retrying the same epic preserves the original goal and queues a fresh continuation.
- Tool result vocabulary is start/resume/queued, never completed/succeeded.
- No child is started and no ticket is mutated merely by calling the tool.

## Do not

- Do not create `bw_run_epic` as an unprefixed or command-shaped alias.
- Do not make the tool a synchronous supervisor, orchestration wrapper, polling loop, or `await_group` equivalent.
- Do not silently select the first ready epic or accept a ticket and walk to its ancestor.
- Do not let children call this tool; it is parent-only alongside Beadwork mutation tools.
- Do not duplicate `/bw run` logic or bypass interrupted-run/goal-exit lifecycle rules.

## Tests and validation

Add focused regressions for schema/discovery, command-tool parity, busy follow-up delivery, idempotent same-goal retry, conflict and validation failures with zero partial mutation, truthful tool details, and no automatic child/ticket mutation. Extend the deterministic in-process acceptance scenario so goal mode begins through the tool rather than a human slash command.

Run:
- `npm run lint -w @solvedbydev/pi-beadwork-extension`
- `npm run test -w @solvedbydev/pi-beadwork-extension`
- `npm run typecheck -w @solvedbydev/pi-beadwork-extension`
- relevant `@solvedbydev/pi-minions` cross-package integration tests

Commit atomically with this issue id.

comments.text: Independent review of 99e8174 PASSed runtime architecture but identified proof/UX gaps. Parent adjudication: FIX/blocking: explicitly dispatch the next `before_agent_start` after tool entry and assert the standing run appendix, because next-turn equivalence is an acceptance behavior; update the epic in-process goal-entry scenario to use `beadwork_start_goal` as the issue explicitly requires (human command parity remains locked by unit tests). FILE/nonblocking but fold into same focused fix: make shared thrown errors surface-neutral rather than saying only `/bw run requires…`; replace tautological cross-session goalId parity with meaningful state/continuation parity. REJECT: busy-parent behavior need not be duplicated in e2e because exact followUp behavior is covered in domain and tool unit tests. Also adapt the one e2e duplicate-workItem all-rejected assertion to expect 8b2.2's intentional rich throw; do not restore success-shaped rejection.

Acceptance complete. Implementation 99e8174 plus fixes 81ee772 and 5dcee29 independently reviewed/re-reviewed PASS. One shared startGoal domain transition powers `/bw run` and `beadwork_start_goal({ epic_id })`; tool entry is explicit, parent-only, truthful started/resumed + continuation disposition, preserves same-goal identity, rejects conflict/validation without partial state, and proves the real next-turn standing appendix. Epic e2e enters via tool; command parity remains unit-tested. Final workspace gates: lint 679 files, tests 437 files / 2235 tests, all-workspace typecheck pass. Closed doors: no inferred tool epic, aliases, synthetic command invocation, child dispatch/ticket mutation, auto-start, polling, await/run-wrapper semantics, or tool-accessible child path.

title: Expose an agent-callable Beadwork goal-mode transition
